_comment: A.S.S. Score 'Slop Roast' copy pools. Config-driven like fingerprints.json: edit copy here, NO code changes needed. One pool per breakdown key (filler, boilerplate, infoDensity, repetitive, crossPage, fingerprints, assets) plus 'clean' for mostly-good sites. Selection (src/roast.js): seeded by the scan id (deterministic, never random); the pool is chosen from the breakdown category that contributed the most weighted points to the overall score (see README 'Slop Roast'). Copy rules: loud/cheeky/meme tone, 1-2 sentences, pattern-based only — never assert AI authorship as fact (no 'was written by AI'-type claims). The mandated disclaimer on every report covers the score itself.

filler.label: AI-style wording
lines: Your copy is 60% buzzwords and 40% confidence in absolutely nothing. Honestly? Impressive.
'Revolutionize the landscape' — bold words from a page that has said nothing yet.
This page talks about synergy so much it might need couples counseling.
Leveraging robust solutions to unlock seamless experiences… ma'am, this is a website.
Your text is so generic it politely introduced itself and then left without saying anything.
Cutting-edge. Seamless. Empower. That's not a paragraph, that's a bingo card.
'In today's fast-paced world' — did you time-travel here from 2014?
Your copy says 'innovative' more often than it says anything else, and we noticed..
Unlock, unleash, elevate — your thesaurus is doing all the writing.
This reads like a mission statement written by a very confident vending machine.
Fifty words of content, forty of them verbs corporate culture told us to love.
You've discovered the secret to saying a great deal of nothing with maximum confidence.
Every sentence is a synonym for 'we exist'. We get it. You exist.
Your homepage runs on 'furthermore', 'moreover', and pure vibes.
This copy is so polished it's slippery. Nothing sticks to it.
Best-in-class, industry-leading, state-of-the-art — and yet, not one single fact.

boilerplate.label: Generic marketing wording
lines: We use cookies to enhance your browsing experience. We also use them because every site says that.
Your legal page has more personality than your homepage, and that is a problem.
Subscribe to our newsletter. Follow us on Twitter. All rights reserved. Copy, paste, and scene.
'We are committed to excellence' — a sentence with the originality of a default printer font.
Your banner says 'your privacy matters to us'. Does it? Or did a template say it first?
This site has generic wording so thick you could build a house out of it.
'Terms and conditions apply' — they always do. Especially to original content, which you've skipped.
The cookie pop-up is the most emotionally expressive part of this website.
Standard legal text, standard marketing text, and in between: nothing custom at all.
Your site reads like every 'About Us' page that was ever copy-pasted.
We value your privacy, we respect your data, and we also ran out of things to say.
'Empowering businesses worldwide' — that exact sentence lives on 40,000 other sites. We saw it on the way here.
Your footer has more compliance links than your content has sentences.
This page is 30% 'get in touch today' and 70% waiting-room ambience.
'We're dedicated to providing the best possible experience' — the conversational equivalent of elevator music.
Seamless onboarding, personalized service, enterprise-grade solutions — presumably one of these is a real thing you do.

infoDensity.label: Thin content — more fluff than facts
lines: Your content is so thin we can see the next page through it.
Every paragraph is two lines long and one of them is a heading. Bold strategy.
This page has the substance of a fortune cookie, minus the enlightenment.
Your site says a lot of words, and none of them are carrying any luggage.
Word salad with extra dressing — and the dressing is also words.
Your about page has the depth of a parking-lot puddle in a drought.
'Elevate your brand' — elevate it to where, exactly? A word cloud?
Short sentences. Shorter paragraphs. Shortest on substance.
This reads like the outline of a website nobody has written yet.
Your content is a smoothie with no fruit in it. It's just ice.
Ten sections, two sentences each, zero facts. Respect the hustle.
The page is all filler and no signal, like a radio station at 3am.
Your text occupies space the way fog does — everywhere, and nothing.
We read your entire homepage in ninety seconds and learned one thing: it exists.
This is the kind of content you skim, then realize you didn't miss anything.
Your copy is a talented mime — lots of gestures, absolutely no words.

repetitive.label: Repeated wording and layouts
lines: Every paragraph starts like the last one. It's a very committed website.
Your page has one idea, and it reintroduces itself at the start of every sentence.
Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, and a prayer that nobody scrolls twice.
Your sentences repeat so often they're practically a chorus now.
Structure-wise, this site is a brick wall that really likes itself.
'We provide', 'we offer', 'we deliver' — was there a fourth one? We'll never know; you ran out.
Your paragraphs are so structurally identical they could be twins. Or clones. Or a typo in the matrix.
Every section is the same rectangle wearing different clip-art energy.
Your content loops like a pre-roll ad you can't skip.
Repeat after us: your site repeats. A lot.
The layout is a grid of same-shaped boxes, and each box says the same thing differently.
Your blog posts are the same post wearing different hats.
Same intro, same rhythm, same everything — this page has commitment issues.
If your page structure were a song, it would be one note, very loud, for a very long time.
Every card, every section, every heading — one layout, infinite reruns.
Your site is like a photocopier that got emotionally attached to page one.

crossPage.label: Same content on multiple pages
lines: Your pages are so similar they should start a podcast called 'We're Basically the Same Site'.
Every page on your site is the same page in a slightly different coat.
Two pages, one content, zero shame.
Your sitemap is less a map and more a list of echoes.
We scanned five pages and found one. The other four were on a loop.
Your about page and your blog share a brain cell — and it's the same sentence.
If your pages were a band, they'd be a cover band covering themselves.
Ninety-eight percent identical? That's not a website, that's a copy shop.
Your site doesn't have pages. It has tabs of the same document.
The front page and the rest of your site are basically roommates at this point.
Your website has one idea, and it's on all five pages holding different doors open.
These pages are so alike they finish each other's — sentences. Because they are the same sentences.
The nav changes, the text doesn't. We noticed. Your visitors notice too.
Your site is one page with delusions of a menu.
We found near-identical pages. We're not mad — just impressed by the commitment to sameness.
Every page on this site went to the same template school and graduated top of its class.

fingerprints.label: Recognizable template design
lines: Your site is wearing a very recognizable template. Fashion-forward? We guess.
A builder's signature is all over this. The autograph is hard to miss.
Your design came from a menu, and it picked the default.
This layout has been seen at 11:30am on 12,000 other sites. Say hi to your twin.
Your site has the vibe of a demo project that never got its custom paint job.
The template says 'trust us, we look professional'. It's been saying that since 2021.
Your design is a hand-me-down from a more confident website.
There's a neon sign above your site flashing 'builder default'. It's subtle.
Your site looks like it came assembled, not designed.
Every element is in its template-approved place. Too approved, honestly.
Your hero section is the same hero we've seen save five thousand other websites.
This site was put together with the precision of someone choosing 'defer to the template'.
Your design says 'we have a brand'. The template says 'we have a template'.
The stock photo of hands shaking is the most authentic thing here.
Generic icon set, gradient hero, rounded cards — the starter pack, fully equipped.
Your site was assembled from an inspiration folder, and the folder was a default theme.

assets.label: Generic images
lines: Your hero image has appeared on forty thousand other websites. Introduce yourself to it.
The filename says it all: image2.png is doing its best.
That 'photo' is so generic it's basically a word, not a picture.
Every image on this page came from a stock photo library, and the library is tired of it.
Your alt-text department filed exactly one report: 'image'. Great work, team.
This gallery was assembled from a folder called 'Free Templates'. We peeked.
spacer.gif is the most honest thing on this page.
A bare 'logo' file, a blank spacer, and zero alt text. Real art.
Your site has more placeholder pixels than a parking lot has empty spaces.
Alt text: 'image'. Image: image. Caption: 'image'. Immersive.
Stock photos are doing 90% of the storytelling here, and they're unionizing.
The template's default gallery found a new home. Congrats to it.
So many generic pictures, the page feels like a showroom for itself.
Every image here came from the same template drawer. Different drawer? No.
image1.jpg, photo2.png and their friend logo.png are running this site now.
We counted more 'image' alt texts than real words on the page. Say hi.

clean.label: Mostly clean
lines: Clean score, clean conscience. Your website barely has any A.S.S. and it shows.
Your site is mostly original, mostly focused, and mostly — we mean this lovingly — not A.S.S.
We dug for slop and found a tidy garden instead. Respect.
Low slop detected. Your website is suspiciously well-behaved.
This site's worst crime is being a little forgettable, and frankly that's fine.
A mostly clean scan — we had to stretch to find something to complain about.
Your website is the designated driver of the internet. Nothing but respect.
Not much A.S.S. here. Almost disappointing. Almost.
The slop meter barely twitched. Your content must have actual thoughts in it.
We came for slop and found a website with actual, real, human-plausible content. We were not prepared.
Your site is fine. Like, genuinely fine. We're a little thrown.
Clean enough that even the template-averse are impressed.
Low on the slop, high on keeping it together. A rare combo.
We rated your website and it did not embarrass itself. Cherish this moment.
Your A.S.S. is minimal today. The internet says thanks.
This page committed no crimes. We checked. Twice.
